staffa.title: The Hebrides
staffa.summary: The Hebrides (; German: Die Hebriden) is a concert overture that was composed by Felix Mendelssohn in 1830, revised in 1832, and published the next year as Mendelssohn's Op. 26. It was inspired by one of Mendelssohn's trips to the British Isles, specifically an 1829 excursion to the Scottish island of Staffa, with its basalt sea cave known as Fingal's Cave.

arran.title: Arran distillery
arran.summary: Lochranza distillery is a whisky distillery in Lochranza, Scotland, on the Isle of Arran. Was founded by Harold Currie, former director of Chivas and a D-Day veteran, with the intention of building a distillery on Arran.

arran.title: Lagg distillery
arran.summary: Lagg distillery is a single malt Scotch whisky distillery located near the village of Lagg, Arran on the southern coast of the Isle of Arran, Scotland. The distillery opened in 2019 and is known for producing heavily peated whiskies.

arran.title: Arran's illicit stills
arran.summary: The Lochranza distillery article says about fifty distilleries once stood on Arran, and that most of them were moonlight or illegal stills.

arran.title: Old Lagg distillery
arran.summary: The Lochranza distillery article says a legal distillery called Lagg on Arran closed in 1837. The same article says a later distillery at Lagg, at the south end of the island, began production in 2019. This row is the closed 1837 still.

isle-of-skye.title: Torabhaig
isle-of-skye.summary: Torabhaig distillery is a Scotch whisky distillery in Teangue on the Isle of Skye. The distillery is the second ever licensed distillery on Skye and the first since Talisker was established in 1830.

isle-of-skye.title: Talisker distillery
isle-of-skye.summary: Talisker distillery is an island single malt Scotch whisky distillery based in Carbost, Scotland on the Minginish Peninsula on the Isle of Skye. The distillery is operated by Diageo and Taliskers’ 10 year old whisky has been nominated as part of their Classic Malts series.

isle-of-skye.title: Illicit stills on Skye
isle-of-skye.summary: At its peak, Skye had seven registered distilleries and many illicit operations. Talisker is one of only two, alongside Torabhaig Distillery, as of 2026.

islay.title: Ardnahoe Distillery
islay.summary: Ardnahoe distillery is a Scotch whisky distillery on Islay, in Scotland.

islay.title: Caol Ila Distillery
islay.summary: Caol Ila distillery is a Scotch whisky distillery near Port Askaig on the isle of Islay, Scotland, owned by Diageo.

islay.title: Port Charlotte distillery
islay.summary: Port Charlotte distillery is an inactive Islay single malt Scotch whisky distillery on the island of Islay, off the west coast of Scotland. The distillery is based in the village of Port Charlotte 3 kilometres (2 miles) southwest from the Bruichladdich distillery.

islay.title: Laphroaig distillery
islay.summary: Laphroaig distillery is a single malt Scotch whisky distillery on Islay, Scotland. It is situated on the south coast of the island, near Port Ellen, at the head of a small bay known as Loch Laphroaig.

islay.title: Bowmore distillery
islay.summary: It is said to have been established in 1779 and is the oldest running distillery on Islay. Bowmore distillery is an Islay single malt Scotch whisky distillery located on the Isle of Islay, an island of the Inner Hebrides.

islay.title: Bunnahabhain Distillery
islay.summary: Bunnahabhain distillery was founded in 1881 near Port Askaig on Islay and is owned by the Scotch whisky producer Distell Group Limited a subsidiary of Heineken N.V,. The village of Bunnahabhain was founded to house its workers.

islay.title: Bruichladdich Distillery
islay.summary: Bruichladdich Distillery is a distillery on the Rhinns of the isle of Islay in Scotland. Originally established in 1881 but closed many times throughout its history, its current form was opened in 2001.

islay.title: Ardbeg
islay.summary: The distillery is owned by Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy, and produces a heavily peated Islay whisky. Ardbeg distillery is an Islay single malt Scotch whisky distillery in Ardbeg on the south coast of the isle of Islay, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, in the Inner Hebrides group of islands.

islay.title: Kilchoman distillery
islay.summary: Kilchoman distillery is a distillery that produces single malt Scotch whisky on Islay, an island of the Inner Hebrides. Kilchoman was founded by Anthony Wills and remains an independent, family run distillery.

islay.title: Lagavulin Distillery
islay.summary: Lagavulin distillery is an Islay single malt Scotch whisky distillery located in the village of Lagavulin on the south of the island of Islay, Scotland. It was previously marketed under the Classic Malts range of single malts, which is now defunct.

islay.title: Port Ellen Distillery
islay.summary: Port Ellen distillery is located in Port Ellen on the isle of Islay, Scotland. Established in 1825 and closed more than once, it reopened in 2024 after having been closed since 1983.

islay.title: Ardenistle distillery
islay.summary: Ardenistle was a distillery on Islay from 1837. It was later called Kildalton, then Islay, and was taken into Laphroaig in 1853.

islay.title: Ardmore (Islay)
islay.summary: Ardmore was a distillery on Islay from 1817 to 1835. Lagavulin took it over in 1837.

islay.title: Daill distillery
islay.summary: Daill was a legal distillery on Islay from 1814 to 1830. The ruins are on the road between Port Askaig and Bridgend.

islay.title: Kildalton distillery
islay.summary: Kildalton was a distillery on Islay from 1817 to 1837, then merged with Lagavulin.

islay.title: Killarow distillery
islay.summary: Killarow was a distillery on Islay from about 1760. From 1818 it was called Bridgend, and it closed in 1822. The ruins are in the village.

islay.title: Lossit distillery
islay.summary: Lossit, later called Ballygrant, was a distillery on Islay. It closed in 1860. The ruins are south of the village, beside the A846.

islay.title: Malt Mill
islay.summary: Malt Mill was a distillery on Islay from 1908 to 1962. The site is now part of Lagavulin.

islay.title: Mulindry distillery
islay.summary: Mulindry was a distillery on Islay in 1826 and 1827, where the Neriby Burn meets the River Laggan. It is now in ruins.

islay.title: Newton distillery (Islay)
islay.summary: Newton was a distillery on Islay from 1819 to 1837. The ruins are beside the road between Port Askaig and Bridgend.

islay.title: Octomore distillery
islay.summary: Octomore was a distillery on Islay from 1816 to 1852. The ruins are near Port Charlotte.

islay.title: Tallant distillery
islay.summary: Tallant was a distillery on Islay from 1821 to 1852, at Tallant farm south of Bowmore.

islay.title: Islay single malts
islay.summary: Islay is one of five Scotch whisky regions whose name is protected by law. The same article says as many as 23 distilleries once worked on the island, and that Bowmore in 1779 is the oldest legal distillery on record there.

islay.title: Fèis Ìle
islay.summary: Islay hosts Fèis Ìle, a festival of malt and music, in the last week of May. The tastings are part of the island's whisky year.

islay.title: Portintruan distillery
islay.summary: Portintruan is a distillery being built on Islay, on the road between Port Ellen and Laphroaig. The article records that work started in 2020. It is not a working distillery yet.

islay.title: Illicit stills on Islay
islay.summary: The Islay single malts article says Irish monks may have distilled on Islay in the early 1300s, and that the island's early distilleries hid in glens and caves when the excise man came. It also records home distilling, smuggling, and illegal whisky production, and says the eight older legal distilleries began as illicit stills.

islay.title: Bunnahabhain village
islay.summary: Bunnahabhain distillery was founded in 1881 near Port Askaig on Islay. The village of Bunnahabhain was founded to house its workers.

islay.summary: Laggan Bay is a malt whisky distillery on Islay, on the shore of Laggan Bay between Bowmore and Port Ellen, near the airport. The Ukrainian Wikipedia article says Ian Macleod Distillers opened it on 2 April 2026, and that it is the eleventh working distillery in the Islay region. mull.title: Ledaig
mull.summary: Tobermory distillery on Mull opened in 1798 under the name Ledaig and later closed more than once. The peated whisky from the same still is still bottled as Ledaig.

osm-relation-7220346.title: Isle of Harris Distillery
osm-relation-7220346.summary: Isle of Harris Distillery is a Scotch whisky and gin distillery in Tarbert on the Isle of Harris, Scotland. The distillery was the first legal distillery ever built on Harris.

mainland-orkney.title: Scapa distillery
mainland-orkney.summary: Scapa distillery is a Scotch whisky distillery on The Mainland of Orkney, Scotland on the shore of Scapa Flow near the town of Kirkwall. Scapa is the third-northernmost whisky distillery in Scotland, 1⁄2 mile (800 metres) south of the Highland Park Distillery.

mainland-orkney.title: Highland Park distillery
mainland-orkney.summary: Highland Park distillery is an Island single malt Scotch whisky distillery located in Kirkwall on the Orkney Islands, Scotland. It is the northernmost single malt Scotch whisky distillery.

mainland-orkney.title: Deerness distillery
mainland-orkney.summary: Deerness distillery is in Deerness on Mainland, Orkney. The Kimbland article describes it as a new Scotch whisky distillery, announced as the first on Orkney since Scapa opened in 1885, a claim Kimbland disputed.

mainland-orkney.summary: Highland Park stands in Kirkwall on Mainland, Orkney. The article says whisky was being distilled illegally on that site in 1798, and that the distillery received a licence in 1826.

osm-relation-3075243.summary: Kimbland distillery is a Scotch whisky and gin micro-distillery located on the Orkney island of Sanday. It claimed to be the most northerly Scotch whisky distillery in the world until the Lerwick Distillery was established in Shetland in 2022.

osm-relation-376677.title: Lerwick Distillery

wd-Q59728286.title: Nun's Island Distillery
wd-Q59728286.summary: Nun's Island Distillery made Irish whiskey on Nun's Island in Galway. The article says it was working from at least 1815, and possibly the late 1700s, until about 1908.

anglesey.title: Anglesey Môn distillery

guernsey.summary: The Guernsey vole (Microtus arvalis sarnius), known in Guernésiais as the mulot, is a subspecies of the common vole endemic to the island of Guernsey in the Channel Islands.

guernsey.title: Loose Flowered orchid
guernsey.summary: Anacamptis laxiflora (lax-flowered orchid, loose-flowered orchid, or green-winged meadow orchid) is a species of orchid. A. laxiflora is common in Normandy and Brittany (France), but in the United Kingdom it is represented only on the Channel Islands, where in Jersey it is called Jersey orchid and in Guernsey it is called Loose Flowered orchid.

isle-of-man.title: red-billed chough
isle-of-man.summary: The red-billed chough, Cornish chough or simply chough ( CHUF; Pyrrhocorax pyrrhocorax) is a bird in the crow family, one of only two species in the genus Pyrrhocorax. P. p. pyrrhocorax, the nominate subspecies and smallest form, is endemic to the British Isles, where it is restricted to Ireland, the Isle of Man, and the west of Wales, southwest Scotland, and Cornwall, which it recolonised in 2001 after an absence of 50 years.

isle-of-man.title: Isle of Man cabbage
isle-of-man.summary: Coincya monensis subsp. monensis, the Isle of Man cabbage, is a species of plant in the family Brassicaceae that is found in coastal habitats on the west of the island of Great Britain (from north Devon to Kintyre) and around the coasts of the Isle of Man. The species was once abundant on the Isle of Man, hence its name, however, for an unknown reason its population has collapsed to only a few individual and isolated plants.

st-kilda.title: St Kilda dandelion
st-kilda.summary: Taraxacum pankhurstianum, also known as the St Kilda dandelion, is a species of dandelion that was identified as new in 2012 after being cultivated at the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh from seeds collected two years previously on the island of Hirta, the largest island in the St Kilda archipelago, on the western edge of Scotland.

st-kilda.title: St Kilda wren
st-kilda.summary: The St Kilda wren (Troglodytes troglodytes hirtensis) is a small passerine bird in the wren family. It is a distinctive subspecies of the Eurasian wren, endemic to the islands of the isolated St Kilda archipelago, in the Atlantic Ocean 64 kilometres (40 mi) west of the Outer Hebrides, Scotland.

st-kilda.title: St Kilda field mouse
st-kilda.summary: The St Kilda field mouse (Apodemus sylvaticus hirtensis) is a subspecies of the wood mouse that is endemic to the Scottish archipelago of St Kilda, the island 64 kilometres (40 mi) west of Benbecula in the Outer Hebrides, and 160 kilometres (100 mi) from mainland Scotland.

fair-isle.title: Fair Isle wren
fair-isle.summary: The Fair Isle wren (Troglodytes troglodytes fridariensis) is a small passerine bird in the wren family. It is a subspecies of the Eurasian wren endemic to Fair Isle, Shetland, Scotland, an island about halfway between mainland Shetland and Orkney.

mainland-shetland.title: Shetland wren
mainland-shetland.summary: The Shetland wren (Troglodytes troglodytes zetlandicus) is a small passerine bird in the wren family. It is a subspecies of the Eurasian wren, endemic to the Shetland archipelago of Scotland, with the exception of Fair Isle which has its own endemic subspecies, the Fair Isle wren.

mainland-shetland.title: Salvelinus gracillimus
mainland-shetland.summary: Salvelinus gracillimus is a cold-water species of fish in the family Salmonidae. The species is endemic to Loch of Girlsta in the Shetland Islands; reports of specimens from Loch More on the Scottish mainland are unconfirmed.

mainland-orkney.title: Orkney vole
mainland-orkney.summary: The Orkney vole (Microtus arvalis orcadensis) is a population of the common vole found in the Orkney Islands, off the northern coast of Scotland.

image.attribution: The original uploader was Karmesinkoenig at English Wikipedia .

osm-relation-2856487.title: Skomer vole
osm-relation-2856487.summary: The Skomer vole (Clethrionomys glareolus skomerensis) is a subspecies of bank vole endemic to the island of Skomer, off the west coast of Wales.

osm-relation-2856487.title: Atlantic puffin
osm-relation-2856487.summary: Skomer (Welsh: Ynys Sgomer) or Skomer Island is an island off the coast of Pembrokeshire, in the community of Marloes and St Brides in west Wales. The Atlantic puffin colony is the largest in southern Britain.

islay.title: Islay shrew
islay.summary: Sorex araneus grantii is a subspecies of the shrew Sorex araneus, found only on the Scottish island of Islay.

lundy.title: Lundy cabbage
lundy.summary: Coincya wrightii, known as Lundy cabbage, is a species of primitive brassicoid, endemic to the island of Lundy off the southwestern coast of England, where it is sufficiently isolated to have formed its own species, with its endemic phytophagous beetles.

lundy.title: Lundy cabbage flea beetle
lundy.summary: Psylliodes luridipennis, commonly known as the Lundy cabbage flea beetle or the bronze Lundy cabbage flea beetle, is a species of flea beetle endemic to the island of Lundy, where it lives and feeds upon the endemic Lundy cabbage (Coincya wrightii).

osm-relation-12597159.title: Orkney charr
osm-relation-12597159.summary: Salvelinus inframundus, also known as Orkney charr, is an extinct cold-water fish in the family Salmonidae which was endemic to Hoy Island, Orkney, Scotland.

arran.title: Arran service-tree
arran.summary: Hedlundia pseudofennica, also called Arran service-tree or Arran cut-leaved whitebeam, is a species of plant in the family Rosaceae. Endemic to the Isle of Arran in Scotland, it is threatened by habitat loss.

arran.title: Arran whitebeam
arran.summary: Hedlundia arranensis, sometimes referred to as the Scottish or Arran whitebeam, is a species of plant in the family Rosaceae. It is endemic to the island of Arran in Scotland.

arran.title: Catacol whitebeam
arran.summary: Hedlundia pseudomeinichii, known as false rowan and Catacol whitebeam, is a rare species of tree endemic to the Isle of Arran in south-western Scotland.

osm-way-4564233.title: Atlantic puffin
osm-way-4564233.summary: Puffin Island (Irish: Oileán na gCánóg), historically called Inishfearglin, is an uninhabited steep rocky island lying off the coast of the Iveragh Peninsula, County Kerry, Ireland. Puffin Island holds important populations of several seabird species, including Atlantic puffins, Manx shearwaters and European storm-petrels, and was acquired as a nature reserve by the Irish Wildbird Conservancy (now BirdWatch Ireland) in the early 1980s.

osm-relation-1146449.title: roseate tern
osm-relation-1146449.summary: The roseate tern (Sterna dougallii) is a species of tern in the family Laridae. The largest European colony, accounting for more than 75% of the European population, is in Ireland, at Rockabill Island, County Dublin.

osm-relation-6045406.title: Shetland mouse-ear
osm-relation-6045406.summary: Cerastium nigrescens var. nigrescens, commonly known as the Shetland mouse-ear, Shetland mouse-eared chickweed or Edmondston's chickweed, is an endemic variety of Arctic Chickweed, Cerastium nigrescens, found in Shetland, Scotland. Although reported from two other sites in the 19th century, it currently grows only on two serpentine hills on the island of Unst.

osm-relation-6045516.title: European dark bee
osm-relation-6045516.summary: Colonsay and Oronsay are home to about 50 colonies of the European dark bee, Apis mellifera mellifera.

osm-way-417926365.title: razorbill
osm-way-417926365.summary: The breeding colonies of razorbills and guillemots on Handa are the largest in the UK, representing 11% and 9% of the total British population respectively.

osm-relation-3198786.title: Least adder's-tongue
osm-relation-3198786.summary: Ophioglossum lusitanicum, the least adder's-tongue, is a small fern of the family Ophioglossaceae. The distribution in Britain is restricted to one small area of coastal heath on St Agnes, Isles of Scilly where it was discovered by John Raven in 1950.

osm-way-30782387.title: Wild peony
osm-way-30782387.summary: Steep Holm and Flat Holm are the only known places in the UK where the wild peony has naturalised.

osm-way-126546636.title: Wild leek
osm-way-126546636.summary: It forms part of the City and County of Cardiff and is now managed by Cardiff Council's Flat Holm Project Team and designated as a Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest and a Special Protection Area, because of the maritime grassland and rare plants such as rock sea-lavender (Limonium binervosum) and wild leek (Allium ampeloprasum).

brownsea.title: Red squirrel
brownsea.summary: The red squirrel (Sciurus vulgaris), also called Eurasian red squirrel, is a species of tree squirrel in the genus Sciurus. Brownsea Island in Poole Harbour is also populated exclusively by red rather than grey squirrels .

osm-way-236730548.title: European storm petrel
osm-way-236730548.summary: What Annet is famous for is its colonies of Manx shearwaters and storm petrels; but since they nest underground, and only come and go in the dark, there is nothing to be seen of them by day.

osm-way-236730548.title: Roccella fuciformis
osm-way-236730548.summary: Annet is the ″British stronghold″ for the lichen Roccella fuciformis.

osm-way-4569485.title: blonde hedgehog
osm-way-4569485.summary: The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus), also known as the West European hedgehog, Western European hedgehog or common hedgehog, is a hedgehog species native to Europe from Iberia and Italy northwards into Scandinavia and westwards into Ireland. They are extremely rare, except on North Ronaldsay and the Channel Island of Alderney, where around 25% of the population is thought to be blonde.

osm-relation-380685.title: Dactylorhiza francis-drucei var. ebudensis
osm-relation-380685.summary: Dactylorhiza francis-drucei is a species of terrestrial orchid native to Great Britain and Ireland. Dactylorhiza francis-drucei var. ebudensis (Wief. ex R.M.Bateman & Denholm) R.M.Bateman & Denholm – North Uist.

isle-of-skye.title: Alpine rock-cress
isle-of-skye.summary: Arabis alpina, the Alpine rock-cress, is a flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae, native to mountainous areas of Europe, North and East Africa, Central and Eastern Asia and parts of North America. In the British Isles, it is only known to occur in a few locations in the Cuillin Ridge of the Isle of Skye.

osm-relation-7230308.title: Edwardsia delapiae
osm-relation-7230308.summary: Edwardsia delapiae is a species of sea anemone which is currently only known from its type locality in south-western Ireland. This species is currently only known from Valentia harbour, County Kerry, Ireland.

osm-way-1043462669.title: Pied avocet
osm-way-1043462669.summary: Havergate Island is an island in the civil parish of Orford, in the East Suffolk district, in the county of Suffolk, England. It is a marshy nature reserve run by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) and is known for its population of pied avocets and terns. The UK's largest breeding population of pied avocets and Suffolk's only breeding Sandwich terns can be found there.

isle-of-wight.title: Red squirrel
isle-of-wight.summary: Although not thought to be under any threat worldwide, the red squirrel has nevertheless drastically reduced in number in the United Kingdom; especially after the eastern grey squirrel was introduced from North America in the 1870s. Fewer than 140,000 individuals are thought to be left in 2013; approximately 85% of which are in Scotland, with the Isle of Wight being the largest haven in England.

osm-relation-6045346.title: South Stack fleawort
osm-relation-6045346.summary: Tephroseris integrifolia subsp. maritima, also known as the spathulate fleawort or South Stack fleawort, is endemic to Holyhead Island, occurring only around South Stack. It is a subspecies of the field fleawort Tephroseris integrifolia.

osm-way-2987757.summary: Access to the island is via a short tidal causeway, which meets the Wales Coast Path long-distance footpath at its Anglesey end.

osm-way-711366463.title: Causeway to Lewis
osm-way-711366463.summary: At low tide Eilean Chaluim Chille is connected by a causeway to the mainland of Lewis at Crobeag.

osm-way-4010134.title: Walked to from the mainland
osm-way-4010134.summary: Eilean Ighe is a small tidal island near Arisaig in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland. Eilean Ighe is one of 43 tidal islands that can be walked to from the mainland of Great Britain and one of 17 that can be walked to from the Scottish mainland.

osm-relation-903616.title: Joined to the other Crowlins
osm-relation-903616.summary: It is situated immediately to the west of Eilean Mòr, and to the north is Eilean Beag, both of which it is connected to at low tide.

osm-way-200758469.title: Walked to from Loch Craignish
osm-way-200758469.summary: Eilean Mhic Chrion is a tidal island sheltering Ardfern in Loch Craignish, Scotland. Eilean Mhic Chrion is one of 43 tidal islands that can be walked to from the mainland of Great Britain and one of 17 that can be walked to from the Scottish mainland.

osm-way-932869382.title: Attached to Glenmore
osm-way-932869382.summary: At low tide it is attached to Glenmore on the Ardnamurchan peninsula.

osm-way-44945730.title: Joined to Coll
osm-way-44945730.summary: It is situated on the western side of Loch Eatharna and is joined to Coll at low tide.

wd-Q5349316.title: Drying sands to Benbecula
wd-Q5349316.summary: At low tide the islands form a peninsula which is connected to Benbecula by drying sands. At high tide the connection to Benbecula is lost.

osm-way-205497205.title: Joined to the other islets
osm-way-205497205.summary: The individual islands are separated from one another at high tide, but connected to one another at low tide, (although not to their much larger neighbour of South Uist).

osm-way-172479890.title: Joined to Scarf's Head
osm-way-172479890.summary: It lies adjacent to a skerry called Scarf's Head, and the two are connected at low tide.

osm-way-4557217.title: Passable only at low tide
osm-way-4557217.summary: It is connected to nearby Castle Island, and thence to the mainland, by a narrow roadway (doran) that is passable only at low tides.

osm-way-252328463.title: Causeway at very low tide
osm-way-252328463.summary: An artificial causeway links the island to the mainland but this is only usable at very low tide.

osm-way-1150257129.title: Joined to the Orkney Mainland
osm-way-1150257129.summary: It is connected to the Orkney Mainland shore at low tide on the opposite side of the bay.

osm-way-41105647.title: Separated at high tide
osm-way-41105647.summary: The islands are connected by a tombolo and are separated at high tide.

osm-way-4011013.title: Joined to Ceann Iar and Ceann Ear
osm-way-4011013.summary: It is tidal, and connected at low tide to Ceann Iar by Fadhail Shibhinis, and to Ceann Ear by Faodhail Chinn Ear.

osm-way-374466281.title: Tombolo to Tiree
osm-way-374466281.summary: At low tide it is joined to mainland Tiree by a sand tombolo and numerous rocky outcrops.

osm-way-39578420.title: Walked to at low tide
osm-way-39578420.summary: It is almost uninhabited, and is usually reached by amphibious craft although, being a tidal island, it is also possible to walk there over the local oyster beds at low tide.

osm-way-108817275.title: Causeway covered at high tide
osm-way-108817275.summary: There is a causeway running to the island that is covered at high tide.

osm-relation-16452553.title: Causeway to Anglesey
osm-relation-16452553.summary: Ynys Faelog is a small tidal island in the Menai Strait between Gwynedd and the Isle of Anglesey, Wales, near the town of Menai Bridge. It is connected by a narrow stone causeway to the Anglesey mainland.

wd-Q542839.title: Road impassable at high tide
wd-Q542839.summary: Spurn is a narrow sand tidal island located off the tip of the coast of the East Riding of Yorkshire, England that reaches into the North Sea and forms the north bank of the mouth of the Humber Estuary. It was a spit with a semi-permanent connection to the mainland, but a storm in 2013 made the road down to the end of Spurn impassable to vehicles at high tide.

osm-relation-2607964.title: Reached on foot at low tide
osm-relation-2607964.summary: It's located around a mile from the shore and, with low tide, can be reached on foot.

osm-way-67823784.title: Causeway at low tide
osm-way-67823784.summary: Following a flood in 1736 Bridgemarsh Island was enclosed by a sea wall and a causeway was built giving access at low tide.

osm-way-401548287.title: Stone causeway to the mainland
osm-way-401548287.summary: Danna (Scottish Gaelic: Danna) is an inhabited tidal island in Argyll and Bute. It is connected to the mainland by a stone causeway.

osm-way-1306669541.title: Joined to Corn Holm
osm-way-1306669541.summary: At low tide it is connected to Corn Holm which is in turn connected to Copinsay by a stretch called "Isle Rough".

osm-relation-16735230.title: Joined to North Uist
osm-relation-16735230.summary: Stromay is joined to North Uist for most of the tidal cycle.

osm-way-157532304.title: Split apart at high tide
osm-way-157532304.summary: At high tide, South Ascrib becomes several smaller land masses cut off from one another (the northernmost one is Eilean Garave).

osm-way-4569263.title: Walked across at very low tide
osm-way-4569263.summary: It is a tidal island that used to be connected to Shapinsay. It is still possible to walk across from the mainland during very low tides.

osm-way-234568444.title: Joined by a tombolo
osm-way-234568444.summary: Ynys y Fydlyn (deutsch Insel Fydlyn) ist eine per Tombolo mit dem Festland verbundene Gezeiteninsel im Nordwesten von Anglesey in Wales in einem dem National Trust gehörenden Küstenabschnitt.

osm-way-4010172.summary: tidal island in the Sound of Arisaig, Moidart, Lochaber, Highland, Scotland, UK

osm-way-191593861.title: Tidal island off St Mary's
osm-way-191593861.summary: tidal island in Isles of Scilly, Cornwall, England, UK

wd-Q40850716.summary: small tidal island off the west coast of Tiree, Argyll and Bute, Scotland, UK

osm-way-413990404.summary: tidal island on North Ronaldsay, Orkney Islands, Scotland, UK

osm-relation-3834460.title: Pennsylvania Castle
osm-relation-3834460.summary: Pennsylvania Castle is a Gothic Revival mansion on the Isle of Portland, Dorset, England. It is located in Wakeham and overlooks Church Ope Cove.

osm-relation-3834460.title: Portland Castle
osm-relation-3834460.summary: Portland Castle is an artillery fort constructed by Henry VIII on the Isle of Portland, Dorset, between 1539 and 1541. It formed part of the King's Device programme to protect against invasion from France and the Holy Roman Empire, and defended the Portland Roads anchorage.

osm-relation-3834460.title: Rufus Castle
osm-relation-3834460.summary: Rufus Castle is a castle on Isle of Portland. The names "Rufus Castle" and "Bow and Arrow Castle" have been widely used since the late 18th Century. It was originally speculated that Rufus referred to King William II, known as William Rufus, however more recent assessments also identify Gilbert de Clare, 7th Earl of Gloucester (the Red Earl) as a possible origin for the name.

guernsey.title: Castle Cornet
guernsey.summary: Castle Cornet is a large island castle in Guernsey, and former tidal island, also known as Cornet Rock or Castle Rock. Its importance was as a defence not only of the island, but of the roadstead.

guernsey.title: Vale Castle
guernsey.summary: Vale Castle, is a protected building located in the Vale, Guernsey. The original name was "Le Château St Michel", later it became "Château de Val" or "Château de Valle" and is over 1,000 years old.

guernsey.title: Château des Marais
guernsey.summary: The Chateau des Marais is a protected chateau in Saint Sampson, Guernsey. The colloquial name is Ivy Castle. A moated medieval castle dating from before the 12th-century.

isle-of-wight.title: Carisbrooke Castle
isle-of-wight.summary: Carisbrooke Castle is a historic motte-and-bailey castle located above, and to the south of, Carisbrooke village centre, on the Isle of Wight, England. Charles I was imprisoned at the castle in the months prior to his trial.

isle-of-wight.title: West Cowes Castle
isle-of-wight.summary: Cowes Castle, also known as West Cowes Castle, is a Device Fort in Cowes on the Isle of Wight. Originally built by Henry VIII in 1539 to protect England against the threat of invasion from France and the Holy Roman Empire, it comprised a circular bastion, flanking wings and a keep, and in 1547 it housed 17 pieces of artillery.

isle-of-wight.title: Sandown Castle
isle-of-wight.summary: Sandown Castle was a Device Fort built at Sandown on the Isle of Wight by Henry VIII in 1545 to protect against the threat of French attack. Constructed from stone with angular bastions, its design was a hybrid of Italian military architectural thinking with traditional English military design.

isle-of-wight.title: Yarmouth Castle
isle-of-wight.summary: Yarmouth Castle is an artillery fort built by Henry VIII in 1547 to protect Yarmouth Harbour on the Isle of Wight from the threat of French attack. Just under 100 feet (30 m) across, the square castle was initially equipped with 15 artillery guns and a garrison of 20 men.

isle-of-wight.title: Norris Castle
isle-of-wight.summary: Norris Castle is located on the Isle of Wight. It was designed by James Wyatt for Lord Henry Seymour.

osm-relation-3969458.title: Southsea Castle
osm-relation-3969458.summary: Southsea Castle, historically also known as Chaderton Castle, South Castle and Portsea Castle, is an artillery fort originally constructed by Henry VIII on Portsea Island, Hampshire, in 1544. It formed part of the King's Device programme to protect against invasion from France and the Holy Roman Empire, and defended the Solent and the eastern approach to Portsmouth.

thames-oxford.title: Oxford Castle
thames-oxford.summary: Oxford Castle is a large, partly ruined medieval castle on the western side of central Oxford in Oxfordshire, England. Most of the original moated, wooden motte and bailey castle was replaced in stone in the late 12th or early 13th century and the castle played an important role in the conflict known as the Anarchy.

osm-way-2957292.title: Elizabeth Castle
osm-way-2957292.summary: Elizabeth Castle is a castle on The Islet. Elizabeth Castle (Norman: Lé Châté Lîzabé) is a castle and tourist attraction, on a tidal island within the parish of Saint Helier, Jersey. Construction was started in the 16th century when the power of the cannon meant that the existing stronghold at Mont Orgueil was insufficient to defend the Island and the port of St Helier was vulnerable to attack by ships armed with cannons.

jersey.title: Mont Orgueil Castle
jersey.summary: Mont Orgueil (French pronunciation: [mɔ̃ ɔʁɡœj]; French for 'Mount Pride') is a castle in Jersey that overlooks the harbour of Gorey; a port on the east coast of the Island. It is known as Gorey Castle by English-speakers, and the "Old Castle" (lé Vièr Châté) by Jèrriais-speakers.

jersey.title: Grosnez Castle
jersey.summary: Grosnez Castle is a ruined 14th-century castle in Saint Ouen, situated on the Grosnez headland in the north-west corner of the island of Jersey in the Channel Islands.

osm-relation-2273838.title: Queenborough Castle
osm-relation-2273838.summary: Queenborough Castle, also known as Sheppey Castle, is a 14th-century castle, the remnants of which are in the town of Queenborough on the Isle of Sheppey, Kent in England. The castle and the associated planned town were built on the orders of King Edward III from 1361 and named in honour his wife, Queen Philippa.

osm-relation-8158173.title: Belvelly Castle
osm-relation-8158173.summary: Belvelly Castle is a 14th or 15th-century tower house in County Cork, Ireland. It is situated next to the small village of Belvelly, opposite and overlooking the only road bridge connecting Fota Island to Great Island (on which the town of Cobh is situated).

scilly-st-marys.title: Ennor Castle
scilly-st-marys.summary: Old Town (Cornish: Treveglos "church town") is a village on St Mary's in the Isles of Scilly located southeast of Hugh Town. It is thought to be the oldest settlement on the island.

scilly-st-marys.title: Star Castle
scilly-st-marys.summary: Star Castle is a castle on St Mary's (Isles of Scilly). Star Castle is a fortress on St Mary's, Isles of Scilly, built in 1593 by Robert Adams, Surveyor of the Royal Works (d.1595) and Francis Godolphin, Captain of the Scilly Isles, during the "Spanish invasion scare."

brownsea.title: Brownsea Castle
brownsea.summary: Brownsea Castle, also known historically as Branksea Castle, was originally a Device Fort constructed by Henry VIII between 1545 and 1547 to protect Poole Harbour in Dorset, England, from the threat of French attack. Located on Brownsea Island, it comprised a stone blockhouse with a hexagonal gun platform.

csv-geocoded-Q24659597.title: St Michael's Mount Castle
csv-geocoded-Q24659597.summary: St Michael's Mount Castle is a castle on St Michael's Mount Castle. St Michael's Mount (Cornish: Karrek Loos yn Koos, meaning grey rock in the woodland) is a tidal island in Mount's Bay, near Penzance, in Cornwall, England. The island is a civil parish and is linked to the town of Marazion by a causeway of granite setts, passable (as is the beach) between mid-tide and low water.

osm-way-169018853.title: Cloghan Castle
osm-way-169018853.summary: Cloghan Castle (Irish: An Clochán) is a ruined tower house on Castle Island in Lough Hyne in West Cork, Ireland. Although it no longer stands, it was originally at least three storeys tall.

osm-way-169018853.title: Castle Island (Carbery West (E.D.) By.) tower house
osm-way-169018853.summary: Castle Island (Carbery West (E.D.) By.) tower house is a castle on Castle Island.

osm-node-8656167145.title: Sketrick Castle
osm-node-8656167145.summary: Sketrick Castle is a castle situated on Sketrick Island near Whiterock, County Down, Northern Ireland. The castle is estimated to date back to the 12th century.

osm-way-3099422.title: Piel Castle
osm-way-3099422.summary: Piel Castle, also known as Fouldry Castle or the Pile of Fouldray, is a castle situated on the south-eastern point of Piel Island, off the coast of the Furness Peninsula in north-west England. Built in the early-14th century by John Cockerham, the Abbot of neighbouring Furness Abbey, it was intended to oversee the trade through the local harbour and to protect against Scottish raids.

osm-way-767535808.title: Cloughoughter Castle
osm-way-767535808.summary: Cloughoughter Castle is a castle on Stony Island.

osm-relation-6188599.title: Granuaile's Castle
osm-relation-6188599.summary: Granuaile's Castle is a tower house and National Monument located in Clare Island, Ireland.

osm-relation-2981832.title: Belle Isle Castle
osm-relation-2981832.summary: Belle Isle Castle is an 18th-century house on Belle Isle, an island previously known, in Gaelic times, as Ballymacmanus Island or Senadh-Mic-Maghnusa or, simply, Senad. The Belle Isle Estate stretches over 470-acres near Lisbellaw in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland.

isle-of-man.title: Greeba Castle
isle-of-man.summary: Greeba Castle is a castle on the Isle of Man.

isle-of-man.title: Castle Rushen
isle-of-man.summary: Castle Rushen (Manx: Cashtal Rosien) is a medieval castle located in the Isle of Man's historic capital, Castletown, in the south of the Island. It towers over the Market Square to the south-east and the harbour to the north-east.

anglesey.title: Beaumaris Castle
anglesey.summary: Castell Biwmares / Beaumaris Castle is a castle on Anglesey (Ynys Môn). Beaumaris Castle ( bew-MAR-is; Welsh: Castell Biwmares, Welsh pronunciation: [kastɛɬ bɪuˈmaːrɛs]), in Beaumaris, Anglesey, Wales, was built as part of Edward I's campaign to conquer north Wales after 1282. Plans were probably first made to construct the castle in 1284, but this was delayed due to lack of funds and work only began in 1295 following the Madog ap Llywelyn uprising.

anglesey.title: Castell Aberlleiniog
anglesey.summary: Castell Aberlleiniog (Welsh for 'castle of the mouth of the Lleiniog') is a motte and bailey fortress near the village of Llangoed on the Isle of Anglesey, in Wales, built between 1080 and 1099 by Hugh d'Avranches, 1st Earl of Chester.

osm-relation-9499902.title: King John's Castle
osm-relation-9499902.summary: King John's Castle (Irish: Caisleán Luimnigh) also known as Limerick Castle is a 13th-century castle located on King's Island in Limerick, Ireland, next to the River Shannon. Although the site dates back to 922 when the Vikings lived on the Island, the castle itself was built on the orders of King John of England in 1200.

csv-geocoded-Q31118312.title: Peel Castle
csv-geocoded-Q31118312.summary: Peel Castle (Cashtal Phurt ny h-Inshey in Manx Gaelic) is a castle in Peel in the Isle of Man, originally constructed by Norwegians. The castle stands on St Patrick's Isle, which is connected to the town by a causeway.

osm-way-115835801.title: Finlaggan Castle
osm-way-115835801.summary: Finlaggan (NR 388 680, Scottish Gaelic: Port an Eilein) is a historic site on Eilean Mòr in Loch Finlaggan, on the island of Islay, around 4 km west of the ferry terminal at Port Askaig.

bute.title: Kilmory Castle
bute.summary: Kilmory Castle (Kilmorie Castle, Crowner's Castle) is the remains of a 15th-century castle at Meikle Kilmory, Isle of Bute, Scotland. The Jamiesons of Kilmorie were the hereditary coroners of Bute.

bute.title: Kames Castle
bute.summary: Kames Castle is a 14th-century tower house located on the shore of Kames Bay near Port Bannatyne, on the Isle of Bute, Scotland. The castle, which is set in 20 acres (81,000 m2) of planted grounds, includes a 2-acre (8,100 m2) 18th-century walled garden.

bute.title: Rothesay Castle
bute.summary: Rothesay Castle is a ruined castle in Rothesay, the principal town on the Isle of Bute, in western Scotland. Located at NS086646, the castle has been described as "one of the most remarkable in Scotland", for its long history dating back to the beginning of the 13th century, and its unusual circular plan.

bute.title: Ascog Castle
bute.summary: Bute, Ascog Castle is a castle on Isle of Bute.

bute.title: Wester Kames Castle
bute.summary: Wester Kames Castle is located near Kames Bay near Port Bannatyne, Isle of Bute, Scotland. Dating from around 1700, the castle was rebuilt around 1900 from a ruined state.

osm-way-4496239.title: Wee Cumbrae Castle
osm-way-4496239.summary: Little Cumbrae Castle sits on Castle Island or Allin Tuirail from the Scottish Gaelic: eilean tùr nan uaislean meaning "islet of the nobles' tower", a small tidal island situated off the east coast of Little Cumbrae, in the Firth of Clyde. It is designated as a scheduled monument.

osm-way-3469292.title: Bass Castle
osm-way-3469292.summary: Bass Castle is a castle on Bass Rock located off the coast of North Berwick, Scotland.

arran.title: Brodick Castle
arran.summary: Brodick Castle is a castle situated outside the port of Brodick on the Isle of Arran, an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland. The castle is a Category A listed building and the grounds are included in the Inventory of Gardens and Designed Landscapes in Scotland.

arran.title: Airds Castle
arran.summary: Airds Castle is a ruined medieval castle near Carradale, Kintyre, Argyll and Bute, Scotland. The castle held a position on the summit of a rocky headland between Carradale harbour and the bay of Port Righ, looking across Kilbrannan Sound to the Isle of Arran.

arran.title: Kildonan Castle
arran.summary: Kildonan Castle stands in the small village of Kildonan on the southern coast of the Isle of Arran in Scotland. The castle's name is derived from the name of a former resident, Saint Donan, who is said to be buried on the island.

arran.title: Lochranza Castle
arran.summary: Lochranza Castle is an L-plan fortified tower house situated on a promontory in Lochranza, on the northern part of the Isle of Arran in Scotland. Most of the current structure was built in the 16th century.

osm-way-562232753.title: Loch Gorm Castle
osm-way-562232753.summary: Loch Gorm Castle is a ruined castle located on Eilean Mòr (big island) on Loch Gorm, Islay, Scotland. It was built in the early 15th century (generally dated to around the 1430s) and served as a stronghold for Clan Donald.

mull.title: Moy Castle
mull.summary: Moy Castle is a ruined castle near Lochbuie on the Isle of Mull, Scotland.

mull.title: Duart Castle
mull.summary: Duart Castle, or Caisteal Dhubhairt in Scottish Gaelic, is a castle on the Isle of Mull, beside the Sound of Mull off the west coast of Scotland, within the council area of Argyll and Bute. The castle dates back to the 13th century and is the seat of Clan MacLean.

mull.title: Aros Castle
mull.summary: Aros Castle, also known as Dounarwyse Castle, is a ruined 13th-century castle near Salen on the Isle of Mull, Scotland.

mull.title: Torosay Castle
mull.summary: Torosay Castle is a large house situated 1+1⁄2 miles (2.5 kilometres) south of Craignure, in the parish of Torosay, on the Isle of Mull, in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.

wd-Q124343695.title: Threave Castle
wd-Q124343695.summary: Threave Castle is a castle on Threave Island. Built in the 1370s by Archibald the Grim, it was a stronghold of the "Black Douglases", Earls of Douglas and Lords of Galloway, until their fall in 1455. For part of this time, the castle and the lordship of Galloway were controlled by Princess Margaret, daughter of Robert III and widow of Archibald Douglas, 4th Earl of Douglas.

osm-relation-4092586.title: Gylen Castle
osm-relation-4092586.summary: Gylen Castle is a ruined castle, or tower house, at the south end of the island of Kerrera in Argyll and Bute, Scotland, on a promontory overlooking the Firth of Lorne. It was made a scheduled monument in 1931.

lindisfarne.title: Lindisfarne Castle
lindisfarne.summary: Lindisfarne Castle is a castle on Lindisfarne (Holy Island). Lindisfarne Castle is a 16th-century castle located on Holy Island, near Berwick-upon-Tweed, Northumberland, England, much altered by Sir Edwin Lutyens in 1901. The island is accessible from the mainland at low tide by means of a causeway.

rathlin.title: Rathlin Castle
rathlin.summary: Rathlin Castle, also known as Bruce's Castle, was a castle on Rathlin Island off the coast of County Antrim in Northern Ireland.

osm-way-495525351.title: Ailsa Craig Castle
osm-way-495525351.summary: Ailsa Craig (; Scottish Gaelic: Creag Ealasaid) is an island of 99 ha (1 km2; 245 acres) in the outer Firth of Clyde, 16 km (8+1⁄2 nmi) west of mainland Scotland. The island's microgranite has long been quarried to make curling stones.

osm-relation-8322850.title: Castle Tarbet
osm-relation-8322850.summary: Castle Tarbet is located on the island of Fidra, East Lothian, within the Firth of Forth, Scotland.

old-lochnaw-castle-w1065572699.title: Old Lochnaw Castle, Isle of Lochnaw
old-lochnaw-castle-w1065572699.summary: Old Lochnaw Castle, Isle of Lochnaw is a castle on Old Lochnaw Castle.

osm-way-115414983.title: Inchgalbraith Castle
osm-way-115414983.summary: Inchgalbraith Castle is a castle on Inchgalbraith.

islay.title: Dunyvaig Castle
islay.summary: Dunyvaig Castle (Scottish Gaelic: Dùn Naomhaig, Anglicised Fort of the galleys, also known as Dunnyveg) is located on the south side of Islay, in Argyll, Scotland, on the shore of Lagavulin Bay, 4 kilometres (2+1⁄2 miles) from Port Ellen. The castle was once a naval base of the Lord of the Isles, chiefs of Clan Donald.

osm-way-60437745.title: Lochleven Castle
osm-way-60437745.summary: Loch Leven Castle is a castle on Castle Island. Lochleven Castle is a ruined castle on an island in Loch Leven, in the Perth and Kinross local authority area of Scotland. Possibly built around 1300, the castle was the site of military action during the Wars of Scottish Independence (1296–1357).

osm-way-985212915.title: Claig Castle
osm-way-985212915.summary: Claig Castle is a castle on Am Fraoch Eilean. It has been classified as a Category C listed building since 23 December 1988.

osm-way-56755400.title: Island I Vow Castle
osm-way-56755400.summary: Island I Vow Castle is a castle on Island I Vow.

osm-way-56755215.title: Inveruglas Isle Castle
osm-way-56755215.summary: Inveruglas Isle Castle is a castle on Inveruglas Ise.

osm-way-8134809.title: Talla Castle
osm-way-8134809.summary: Talla Castle, also known as Inch Talla or Inchtalla Castle, was a 15th-century castle on Inchtalla upon Lake of Menteith, Scotland. The castle was built by Malise Graham, Earl of Mentieth starting in 1427.

osm-relation-5497270.title: Inch Castle
osm-relation-5497270.summary: Inch Castle is a ruined castle located on the southern tip of Inch Island in County Donegal in Ulster, the northern province in Ireland. The castle was constructed around 1430 by the Gaelic Irish lord Neachtain O'Donnell for his father-in-law, Cahir O'Doherty.

osm-way-205258734.title: Innes Chonnel Castle
osm-way-205258734.summary: Innes Chonnel Castle is a castle on Innischonnell. Innes Chonnel Castle or Ardchonnel Castle is a ruined 13th-century castle on Innis Chonnell, an island on Loch Awe near Dalavich, Argyll and Bute, Scotland. The fortress was once a stronghold of Clan Campbell.

osm-way-4010491.title: Kisimul Castle
osm-way-4010491.summary: Kisimul Castle is a castle on Ciosmul. Kisimul Castle (Scottish Gaelic: Caisteal Chiosmuil) and also known as Kiessimul Castle, is a medieval castle located on a small island off Castlebay, Barra, in the Outer Hebrides, Scotland. It gets its name from the Norse ciosamul, meaning "castle island".

osm-way-4010491.title: Caisteal Chiosmuil
osm-way-4010491.summary: Caisteal Chiosmuil is a castle on Ciosmul. Kisimul Castle (Scottish Gaelic: Caisteal Chiosmuil) and also known as Kiessimul Castle, is a medieval castle located on a small island off Castlebay, Barra, in the Outer Hebrides, Scotland. It gets its name from the Norse ciosamul, meaning "castle island".

image.attribution: Conor Lawless from North Uist, United Kingdom

csv-geocoded-Q217058.title: Castle Stalker
csv-geocoded-Q217058.summary: Castle Stalker (Scottish Gaelic: Caisteal an Stalcaire) is a four-storey tower house or keep in the Scottish county of Argyll. It is set on a tidal islet on Loch Laich, an inlet off Loch Linnhe.

isle-of-skye.title: Caisteal Maol
isle-of-skye.summary: Caisteal Maol (Gaelic: Caisteal, 'Castle', Maol, 'bare') is a ruined castle located near the harbour of the village of Kyleakin, Isle of Skye, Scotland. It is also known as Castle Moil, Castle Maol, Dun Akyn, Dunakin Castle, Dun Haakon and Castle Dunakin.

isle-of-skye.title: Knock Castle
isle-of-skye.summary: Knock Castle, also known as Caisteal Chamuis (Castle Camus) is a former stronghold of Clan MacLeod of Lewis and later, MacDonalds. It lies on the east coast of Sleat, approximately five miles (8.0 km) north of Armadale on the Isle of Skye, south of Cnoc Uaine, on the eastern side of Knock Bay.

image.attribution: http://www.isleofskye.com/tour/sleat/ Originally uploaded to w:File:KnockCastle1.jpg by w:User:Mjgm84

isle-of-skye.title: Dunscaith Castle
isle-of-skye.summary: Dunscaith Castle also known as Dun Scaich, Dun Sgathaich Castle and Tokavaig, is a ruined castle on the coast of the Isle of Skye, in the north-west of Scotland. It is located in the Parish of Sleat, in the Highland council area, and in the former county of Inverness-shire, at grid reference NG595120.

isle-of-skye.title: Dunvegan Castle
isle-of-skye.summary: Dunvegan Castle (Caisteal Dhùn Bheagain) is located 1 mile (1.6 km) to the north of Dunvegan on the Isle of Skye, off the west coast of Scotland. It is the seat of the MacLeod of MacLeod, chief of the Clan MacLeod.

isle-of-skye.title: Duntulm Castle
isle-of-skye.summary: Duntulm Castle stands ruined on the north coast of Trotternish, on the Isle of Skye in Scotland, near the hamlet of Duntulm.

osm-way-205500003.title: Calvay Castle
osm-way-205500003.summary: Calvay Castle (Scottish Gaelic: Caisteal Calbhaigh) is a ruined castle on an islet close to the island of Calbhaigh, at the eastern approaches to Loch Boisdale, South Uist. The castle is linked by a causeway from Calbhaigh, which becomes inundated at high tide.

castle-island-w223640455.title: Kinord Castle
castle-island-w223640455.summary: Kinord Castle, also known as Loch Kinord Castle, was a 14th-century castle on Castle Island in Loch Kinord to the south of Old Kinord, Aberdeenshire, Scotland.

osm-way-205118309.title: Castle Shuna
osm-way-205118309.summary: Castle Shuna is a castle on Shuna Island.

osm-way-4009288.title: Castle Tioram
osm-way-4009288.summary: Castle Tioram (; Scottish Gaelic: Caisteal Tioram, meaning "dry castle") is a ruined castle that sits on the tidal island Eilean Tioram in Loch Moidart, Scotland. Though hidden from the sea, the castle controls access to Loch Shiel.

osm-way-4009559.title: Cairnburgh Castle
osm-way-4009559.summary: Cairnburgh Castle is a ruined castle that is located on the islands of Cairn na Burgh Mòr and Cairn na Burgh Beag, Argyll and Bute, Scotland. 1991's The Changing Scottish Landscape characterizes it as "one of the most isolated fortifications in Britain...[and] also one of the strangest."

osm-relation-1663893.title: Brochel Castle
osm-relation-1663893.summary: Brochel Castle is a ruined castle located on a 15-metre-high rocky pinnacle on the north-eastern shore of Raasay, in the council area of Highland, Scotland.

osm-relation-5420246.title: Old Breachacha Castle
osm-relation-5420246.summary: Breachacha Castle (also spelled Breacachadh) is either of two structures on the shore of Loch Breachacha, on the Inner Hebridean island of Coll, Scotland. The earlier (also called Old Breachacha Castle) is a 15th-century tower house that was a stronghold of the Macleans of Coll, the island having been granted to John Maclean in 1431.

osm-relation-5420246.title: Breachacha Castle
osm-relation-5420246.summary: Coll, Breachacha Castle is a castle on Coll.

osm-relation-380684.title: Borve Castle
osm-relation-380684.summary: Borve Castle, also known as Castle Wearie, and Caisteal Bhuirgh in Scottish Gaelic, is a ruined 14th-century tower house, located at the south-west of the island of Benbecula, in the Western Isles of Scotland. The castle was designated as a Scheduled Monument in 1993.

wd-Q43372925.title: Lochindorb Castle
wd-Q43372925.summary: In the loch there is an island, which is now thought to have been artificially created, and on that island are the ruins of Lochindorb Castle, a former stronghold of the Clan Comyn. King Edward I of England stayed in the castle during his 1303 campaign against the Scots.

osm-way-201511514.title: Eilean Donan Castle
osm-way-201511514.summary: Eilean Donan (Scottish Gaelic: Eilean Donnain) is a small tidal island situated at the confluence of three sea lochs (Loch Duich, Loch Long and Loch Alsh) in the western Highlands of Scotland, about one kilometre (5⁄8 mi) from the village of Dornie. It is connected to the mainland by a footbridge that was installed early in the 20th century and is dominated by a picturesque castle that frequently appears in photographs, film and television.

osm-relation-376677.title: Scalloway Castle
osm-relation-376677.summary: Scalloway Castle is a tower house in Scalloway, on the Shetland Mainland, the largest island in the Shetland Islands of Scotland. The tower was built in 1600 by Patrick Stewart, 2nd Earl of Orkney, during his brief period as de facto ruler of Shetland.

osm-relation-3148465.title: Noltland Castle
osm-relation-3148465.summary: Noltland Castle is located near Pierowall on the island of Westray in the Orkney Islands of Scotland. It dates mainly to the later 16th century, although it was never fully completed.

osm-relation-6045406.title: Muness Castle
osm-relation-6045406.summary: Muness Castle is located on Unst, which is one of the Shetland Islands of Scotland. Unst is Scotland's most northerly inhabited island, and Muness is the most northerly fortalice in the British Isles.

mainland-orkney.title: Kirkwall Castle
mainland-orkney.summary: Kirkwall Castle is a castle on Mainland (Orkney). Kirkwall Castle, also known as King's Castle, was located in Kirkwall, the main settlement in the Orkney Islands of Scotland. Built in the 14th century, it was deliberately destroyed in 1614.

osm-relation-12597289.title: Balfour Castle
osm-relation-12597289.summary: Balfour Castle is a historic building on the southwest of Shapinsay, Orkney Islands. Though built around an older structure that dates at least from the 18th century, the present castle was built in 1847, commissioned by Colonel David Balfour, and designed by Edinburgh architect David Bryce.

osm-relation-3214114.title: Cromwell's Castle
osm-relation-3214114.summary: Cromwell's Castle is an artillery fort overlooking New Grimsby harbour on the island of Tresco in the Isles of Scilly. It comprises a tall, circular gun tower and an adjacent gun platform, and was designed to prevent enemy naval vessels from entering the harbour.

osm-relation-3214114.title: King Charles's Castle
osm-relation-3214114.summary: King Charles's Castle is a ruined artillery fort overlooking New Grimsby harbour on the island of Tresco in the Isles of Scilly.

osm-relation-3235264.title: O'Brien's Castle
osm-relation-3235264.summary: O'Brien's Castle, also called Furmina Castle, is an early 15th century tower house and National Monument located on Inisheer, Ireland.

osm-way-355520866.title: Kilcoe Castle
osm-way-355520866.summary: Kilcoe Castle is a 15th-century coastal tower house located on a 0.81 ha (2 acres) island, called Mannin Beg, in the Kilcoe townland in Roaringwater Bay in West Cork, Ireland.

osm-relation-6045364.summary: Carrickkildavnet Castle or Kildavnet Castle is a tower house and National Monument located in Achill Island, Ireland.

osm-way-4557019.title: Mahee Castle
osm-way-4557019.summary: Mahee Castle, also known as Nendrum Castle, is a small ruined tower house near Nendrum Monastery on Mahee Island in Strangford Lough, County Down, Northern Ireland.

lundy.title: Marisco Castle
lundy.summary: Henry III built the castle (sometimes referred to as the Marisco Castle) in an attempt to establish the rule of law on the island and its surrounding waters. In the English Civil War, Thomas Bushell held Lundy for King Charles I, rebuilding Marisco Castle and garrisoning the island at his own expense.

jersey.title: The Battle of the Strong
jersey.summary: The Battle of the Strong is an 1898 novel by Gilbert Parker. The book is set in the Channel Islands, primarily during the period 1781-95, and opens with attempted invasion of Jersey by France in the Battle of Jersey.

jersey.title: Night of the Fox
jersey.summary: Night of the Fox is a World War II spy thriller novel by Jack Higgins, first published in 1986. He is washed ashore on Jersey, and rescued by Hélène de Ville, wife of the Seigneur of Jersey, and Sean Gallagher, a former General in the Irish Army, who has retired in Jersey.

wd-Q27508141.title: The Bondman
wd-Q27508141.summary: The Bondman is an 1890 best-selling novel by Hall Caine set in the Isle of Man and Iceland.

wd-Q27508141.title: The Deemster
wd-Q27508141.summary: The Deemster is a novel by Hall Caine published in 1887, considered to be the first 'Manx novel'. It was Caine's third novel, the second to be set in the Isle of Man and it was his first great success.

wd-Q27508141.title: The Manxman
wd-Q27508141.summary: The Manxman is a novel by Hall Caine, first appearing as a serial in The Queen, The Lady's Newspaper and Court Chronicle between January and July 1894. A highly popular novel of its period, it was set in the Isle of Man and concerned a romantic triangle.

wd-Q27508141.title: Peveril of the Peak
wd-Q27508141.summary: Peveril of the Peak (1823) is the longest novel by Walter Scott. Most of the story takes place in Derbyshire, London, and on the Isle of Man.

wd-Q27508141.title: She's All the World to Me
wd-Q27508141.summary: She's All The World To Me is a short early novel by Hall Caine published in 1885 by Harper & Brothers. The novel was the first of Caine's works to be set on the Isle of Man and it centered on themes that would become integral to his later novels: a love triangle, secret mounting sins and eventual redemption.
wd-Q27508141.sourceTitle: She's All the World to Me

wd-Q27508141.title: The Woman of Knockaloe
wd-Q27508141.summary: The Woman of Knockaloe: A Parable is a melodramatic novel by Hall Caine first published in 1923. Set on the Isle of Man during the First World War, a young woman finds herself drawn to one of the nearby German internees.

osm-way-3469292.title: Catriona
osm-way-3469292.summary: Catriona (also known as David Balfour) is an 1893 novel written by Robert Louis Stevenson as a sequel to his earlier novel Kidnapped (1886). However, his attempts fail, as after being reunited with Alan Breck he is once again kidnapped, and held on the Bass Rock, an island prison in the Firth of Forth, until the trial is over, and James is condemned to death.

guernsey.title: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society
guernsey.summary: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society is a historical novel by Mary Ann Shaffer and Annie Barrows that was published in 2008. Isola Pribby, a member of the Society, believes that Dawsey is in love with Remy and, using Miss Marple as a model, offers to clean Dawsey's home to find proof he is in love with Remy to convince her to stay in Guernsey.
guernsey.sourceTitle: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society

guernsey.title: Just War
guernsey.summary: Just War is a novel by Lance Parkin from the Virgin New Adventures. The story is set in Nazi Germany-occupied Guernsey, an example of invasion literature.

guernsey.title: Toilers of the Sea
guernsey.summary: Toilers of the Sea (French: Les Travailleurs de la mer) is a novel by Victor Hugo published in 1866. A woman arrives in Guernsey, with her son Gilliat, and buys a house said to be haunted.

image.attribution: Illustration by François Chifflart ; wood-engraved by Fortuné Méaulle

osm-relation-9603390.title: John of John
osm-relation-9603390.summary: John of John is a 2026 novel by Scottish-American author Douglas Stuart. The novel is set on the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland during the late 1990s.

osm-relation-9620215.title: Kidnapped
osm-relation-9620215.summary: Kidnapped is a historical fiction adventure novel by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson, written as a boys' novel and first published in the magazine Young Folks from May to July 1886. David and Alan are separated in the confusion, with David being washed ashore on the isle of Erraid, near Mull, while Alan and the surviving crew row to safety on that same island.

osm-relation-3217444.title: Listen to the Moon
osm-relation-3217444.summary: Listen to the Moon is a British children's novel written by Michael Morpurgo. Young Alfie Wheatcroft, his parents Jim and Mary and Uncle Billy live on the island of Bryher, and make a living by fishing and farming.

osm-relation-3217444.title: The Wreck of the Zanzibar
osm-relation-3217444.summary: The Wreck Of The Zanzibar is a children's novel written by Michael Morpurgo. She tells of her life on Bryher, one of Britain's Scilly Isles, where her family's survival depends on the mercy of the elements and the sea.

osm-relation-3217444.title: Why the Whales Came
osm-relation-3217444.summary: Why the Whales Came is a British children's story written by Michael Morpurgo. It was first published in 1985 in the United Kingdom by William Heinemann, and by Scholastic in the United States. It is set on the island of Bryher, one of the Isles of Scilly, off the coast of Cornwall, in the year 1914.

rockall.title: The Master: An Adventure Story
rockall.summary: The Master: An Adventure Story is a 1957 science fiction adventure novel by English author T. H. White. It involves two children, Judy and Nicky, and their dog Jokey, who are stranded on Rockall, an extremely small, uninhabited, remote rocky islet in the North Atlantic Ocean.

mainland-orkney.title: The Outrun
mainland-orkney.summary: The Outrun is a 2016 memoir by the Scottish journalist and author Amy Liptrot. It is set in Orkney, her childhood home, where she returned to rehabilitate after becoming an alcoholic in London.

mainland-orkney.title: The Stronghold
mainland-orkney.summary: The Stronghold is a children's historical novel by the Scottish writer Mollie Hunter, published by Hamilton in 1974. Set in the Orkney islands during the 1st century BC, the story is an imaginative reconstruction of the development of the broch, the circular stronghold design of fortifications that dot the islands.

mainland-orkney.title: Vinland
mainland-orkney.summary: Vinland, published in 1992 by George Mackay Brown, is a historical novel set in the Orkney Islands in the early 11th century.

osm-way-2956937.title: Mr Pye
osm-way-2956937.summary: Mr Pye is a 1953 novel by English novelist Mervyn Peake, first published by Heinemann. Mr. Pye travels to the Channel Island of Sark to awaken a love of God in all the islanders.

osm-way-2956937.title: Carette of Sark
osm-way-2956937.summary: John Oxenham wrote Carette of Sark (1907) and The Perilous Lovers (1924), historical novels largely set on Sark.

osm-way-2956937.title: The Perilous Lovers
osm-way-2956937.summary: John Oxenham wrote Carette of Sark (1907) and The Perilous Lovers (1924), historical novels largely set on Sark.

osm-way-2956937.title: A Maid of the Silver Sea
osm-way-2956937.summary: Little Sark is a peninsula joined by a natural but high and very narrow isthmus to the rest of Sark Island. His 1910 novel A Maid of the Silver Sea uses the mines of Little Sark as its setting.

osm-way-2956937.title: Dame of Sark
osm-way-2956937.summary: Dame of Sark, the memoirs of the 21st Seigneur Sibyl Mary Hathaway, who was present during the German occupation, were made into a play and television drama of the same name. Dame Sibyl also wrote Maid of Sark, an historical romance published in 1939; set in the sixteenth century, it incorporates events related to the defence of the island against the Bretons.

osm-way-2956937.title: The Last Kings of Sark
osm-way-2956937.summary: The Last Kings of Sark: A Novel by Rosa Rankin-Gee is a 2015 coming-of-age story set in Sark.

osm-way-2956937.title: Iron Chamber of Memory
osm-way-2956937.summary: The 2016 novel Iron Chamber of Memory by John C. Wright is set in Sark.

isle-of-skye.title: To the Lighthouse
isle-of-skye.summary: To the Lighthouse is a 1927 novel by Virginia Woolf. The novel centres on the Ramsay family and their visits to the Isle of Skye in Scotland between 1910 and 1920.

isle-of-skye.title: Wildfire at Midnight
isle-of-skye.summary: Wildfire at Midnight is a novel by Mary Stewart which was first published in 1956. Fashion model Gianetta Brooke goes on holiday to the Scottish island of Skye, only to find that her ex-husband, writer Nicholas Drury, is staying at the same hotel in Camasunary.

isle-of-skye.title: The Hill of the Red Fox
isle-of-skye.summary: McLean was the writer of a number of children's novels: The Hill of the Red Fox (1955; a contemporary spy story set in Skye); The Man of the House (1956; known as Storm over Skye in the US); Ribbon of Fire (1962; also set in Skye around the time of the Highland Clearances); Master of Morgana (1965); The Year of the Stranger (1971); and A Sound of Trumpets (1971).

isle-of-skye.title: Ribbon of Fire
isle-of-skye.summary: McLean was the writer of a number of children's novels: The Hill of the Red Fox (1955; a contemporary spy story set in Skye); The Man of the House (1956; known as Storm over Skye in the US); Ribbon of Fire (1962; also set in Skye around the time of the Highland Clearances); Master of Morgana (1965); The Year of the Stranger (1971); and A Sound of Trumpets (1971).

st-kilda.title: Where the World Ends
st-kilda.summary: Where the World Ends is a 2017 young adult novel by British writer Geraldine McCaughrean and illustrated by Jane Milloy. Set in 1727 on the remote St Kilda archipelago in northern Scotland, the book follows a group of nine boys and three men who are abandoned on a sea stack while harvesting birds for an annual tradition.

isle-of-wight.title: The Trespasser (Lawrence novel)
isle-of-wight.summary: The Trespasser is a 1912 novel by D. H. Lawrence. Set mostly on the Isle of Wight, it tells the story of Siegmund, a married man with children, and his adulterous affair with Helena.

isle-of-wight.title: The Night of the Triffids
isle-of-wight.summary: The Night of the Triffids is a science fiction novel by British writer Simon Clark, published in 2001. The story begins on the Isle of Wight, 25 years after the events from The Day of the Triffids.

isle-of-wight.title: England, England
isle-of-wight.summary: England, England is a satirical postmodern novel by Julian Barnes, published and shortlisted for the Booker Prize in 1998. Martha is now in her forties and is employed by the entrepreneur Sir Jack Pitman for a megalomaniacal project: Sir Jack aims to turn the Isle of Wight into a gigantic theme park which contains everything that people, especially tourists, consider to be quintessentially English, selected according to what Sir Jack himself approves of.

osm-relation-2273838.title: Wide Open
osm-relation-2273838.summary: Wide Open is the third novel by English author Nicola Barker published in 1998 by Faber and Faber. Set mostly on the Isle of Sheppey on the north coast of Kent on the Thames Estuary.

scilly-st-marys.title: The Sleeping Sword
scilly-st-marys.summary: The Sleeping Sword is a British children's novel written by Michael Morpurgo, and illustrated by Michael Foreman. The sword found on the island of Bryher, inspired Morpurgo's Arthurian tale, set in the Scilly Isles, and is a story within a story.

osm-way-61921366.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
osm-way-61921366.summary: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter is a novel by Hazel Gaynor. It is set in two main locations: Longstone Lighthouse on the Northumberland Coast in England in the late 1830s and early 1840s, for which Gaynor uses historical fiction to describe the experiences of Grace Darling; and Newport, Rhode Island, particularly the Rose Island Light, in which the main protagonist is a fictional character in the late 1930s, Matilda Emmerson.

rathlin.title: Turbulent Priests
rathlin.summary: Turbulent Priests is the third novel of the Dan Starkey series by Northern Irish author, Colin Bateman, released on 6 December 1999 through HarperCollins. Bateman's usage of Rathlin Island (which he renamed "Wrathlin Island" in the novel) as the book's setting led to Bateman being invited to unveil a "Writer's Chair", commemorating writers of all origin and genre.

mainland-shetland.title: A Stranger Came Ashore
mainland-shetland.summary: A Stranger Came Ashore is a 1975 young adult novel written by Scottish author Mollie Hunter. Set in the Shetland Islands in the north of Scotland, the plot revolves around a boy called Robbie Henderson, his family and a mysterious stranger named Finn Learson.

mainland-shetland.title: Raven Black
mainland-shetland.summary: Raven Black is a 2006 novel by Ann Cleeves that won the Duncan Lawrie Dagger Award for the best crime novel of the year. Raven Black is the first in the "Shetland" mysteries, a series of eight novels by Cleeves, composed of two quartets, all set in Shetland.

mainland-shetland.title: The Pirate
mainland-shetland.summary: The Pirate (published at the end of 1821 with the date 1822) is one of the Waverley novels by Sir Walter Scott, based roughly on the life of John Gow who features as Captain Cleveland. The setting is the southern tip of the main island of Shetland (which Scott visited in 1814), towards the end of the 17th century, with 1689 as the likely date of the main incidents.

osm-way-4009637.title: Bridal Path
osm-way-4009637.summary: Bridal Path is a novel by Scottish author Nigel Tranter, first published in 1952. The story begins on Eorsa, an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland.

osm-relation-3601567.title: Venus as a Boy
osm-relation-3601567.summary: Venus as a Boy is a 2004 fiction novella by Scottish writer and musician Luke Sutherland, his third publication following two earlier novels, Jelly Roll (1998) and Sweetmeat (2002). It is set briefly in South Ronaldsay, Orkney, an island off the coast of Scotland though it is largely set in Soho, London.

osm-relation-6045552.title: Over the Bar
osm-relation-6045552.summary: Over the Bar: A Personal Relationship with the GAA is a memoir by the Irish writer Breandán Ó hEithir, describing his early life on Inishmore, his education at University College, Galway (where he subsequently dropped out) and his long-time involvement with the Gaelic Athletic Association.

osm-relation-6045552.title: An Aran Keening
osm-relation-6045552.summary: Andrew McNeillie (born 12 August 1946) is a British poet and literary editor. His prose memoir An Aran Keening tells of his stay on Inis Mór, just short of a year through 1968 and 1969.

lewis-and-harris.title: The Blackhouse
lewis-and-harris.summary: The Blackhouse is a suspense thriller, the first novel of The Lewis Trilogy, written by the Scottish writer Peter May. The action takes place mostly on the remote and weather-beaten Isle of Lewis off the coast of northern Scotland.

lewis-and-harris.title: Great Northern?
lewis-and-harris.summary: Great Northern? is the twelfth and final completed book of Arthur Ransome's Swallows and Amazons series of children's books. Ransome also made a visit to the Isle of Lewis in the Outer Hebrides for a fishing trip and to research the area as the setting for the book.

osm-relation-6046655.title: Tide-race
osm-relation-6046655.summary: She won the first two Gold Medals awarded by the National Eisteddfod of Wales in the Fine Art category, for her paintings Girl with a Siamese Cat (1951) and The Cristin Children (1953), and her written works include Tide-race, a memoir of 15 years spent living on Bardsey Island.

osm-relation-6046655.title: The Bones Beneath
osm-relation-6046655.summary: Crime writer Mark Billingham set his 2014 novel, The Bones Beneath, on Bardsey. He includes notes on the island at the end of the book, which is one in his series of Tom Thorne novels.

osm-relation-6046655.title: Twenty Thousand Saints
osm-relation-6046655.summary: Since 1999, the Bardsey Island Trust has appointed an 'Artist in Residence' to spend several weeks on the island producing work which is later exhibited on the mainland. A Welsh literary residence was created in 2002; singer-songwriter Fflur Dafydd spent six weeks working on a collection of poetry and prose. Her play Hugo was inspired by her stay, and she has produced two novels, Atyniad (English: Attraction), which won the prose medal at the 2006 Eisteddfod; and Twenty Thousand Saints, winner of the Oxfam Hay Prize, which tells how the women of the island, starved of men, turn to each other.

osm-way-2956897.title: Where Seagulls Dare
osm-way-2956897.summary: Herm (Guernésiais: Haerme, ultimately from Old Norse armr 'arm', due to the shape of the island, or Old French eremite 'hermit') is one of the Channel Islands and part of the Parish of St Peter Port in the Bailiwick of Guernsey. Paul Sherman has written two collections of short stories set on the island: Where Seagulls Dare and One Flew Over the Puffin's Nest.

osm-way-2956897.title: One Flew Over the Puffin's Nest

Paul Sherman has written two collections of short stories set on the island: Where Seagulls Dare and One Flew Over the Puffin's Nest.

osm-relation-12913146.title: A Line to Kill
osm-relation-12913146.summary: Alderney ( AWL-dər-nee; French: Aurigny [oʁiɲi]; Auregnais: Aoeur'gny) is the northernmost of the inhabited Channel Islands. In the 2021 novel A Line to Kill by Anthony Horowitz, the island is featured as the setting. In which, during the island's Alderney Literary Festival, a murder takes place.

osm-relation-3214114.title: Hell Bay
osm-relation-3214114.summary: Tresco (Cornish: Enys Skaw, lit. 'island of elder-trees') is the second-biggest island of the Isles of Scilly. Hell Bay (1984), by Sam Llewellyn, is set on Tresco and fictionalises the events leading up to Augustus Smith taking ownership of the island.

osm-relation-6188599.title: The Ghost of Grania O'Malley
osm-relation-6188599.summary: Clare Island (Irish: Cliara or Oileán Chliara), also historically Inishcleer, is a mountainous island guarding the entrance to Clew Bay in County Mayo, Ireland. Historically part of the kingdom of Umhaill, it is famous as the home of the 16th century pirate queen Gráinne O'Malley. Clare Island is the setting for the Michael Morpurgo book The Ghost of Grania O'Malley.

osm-way-376497843.title: Stargazing: Memoirs of a Young Lighthouse Keeper
osm-way-376497843.summary: Stargazing: Memoirs of a Young Lighthouse Keeper is a autobiographical book by Peter Hill published in 2003 by Canongate Books. In January 2004, it was BBC Radio 4's Book of the Week read by David Tennant, and received the Saltire Society's First Book of the Year Award in December that year. The book is a memoir about Hill's time in the early 1970s as a young lighthouse keeper on the remote Scottish coast at the Pladda Lighthouse, Ailsa Craig Lighthouse, and the Hyskeir Lighthouse.
osm-way-376497843.sourceTitle: Stargazing: Memoirs of a Young Lighthouse Keeper

osm-way-4569530.title: The Outrun
osm-way-4569530.summary: The Outrun is a 2016 memoir by the Scottish journalist and author Amy Liptrot. It is set in Orkney, her childhood home, where she returned to rehabilitate after becoming an alcoholic in London. Later, she spends a winter on the Orkney island of Papa Westray in the RSPB's house, which is normally only used in summer.

osm-way-30782387.title: Arcam
osm-way-30782387.summary: The island is the focal point of the 2018 crime thriller Arcam, by Jason Minick.

mainland-shetland.title: Up Helly Aa
mainland-shetland.summary: Up Helly Aa (Shaetlan pronunciation: [ˌɔp hɛli ˈaː] UP-hel-ee-AH; literally "Up Holy [Day] All") is a type of fire festival held annually from January to March in various communities in Shetland, Scotland, to mark the end of the Yule season. Each festival involves a torchlit procession by squads of costumed participants (known as guizers) that culminates in the burning of an imitation Viking galley.

mainland-shetland.title: Delting Up Helly Aa
mainland-shetland.summary: Delting Up Helly Aa (known as Brae Up Helly Aa until 2001) is the final festival in the Shetland Islands' Up Helly Aa calendar, taking place on the third Friday of March in the parish of Delting. It has been held in the Mossbank Community Hall with the Manager of Sullom Voe Terminal since 1999.

mainland-shetland.title: Ness yoal
mainland-shetland.summary: The yoal (Shaetlan pronunciation: [joɐɫ] YOHL), often referred to as the ness yoal, is a clinker-built craft used traditionally in Shetland, Scotland. However, the Ness yoal is better regarded as a successful and sophisticated adaptation for the specific local requirements of the fishermen where these vessels were used which was Dunrossness, the southernmost parish of Mainland.

mainland-orkney.title: The Ba
mainland-orkney.summary: The Kirkwall Ba' Game (known locally as The Ba') is one of the main annual events held in the town of Kirkwall, in Orkney, Scotland. It is one of a number of Ba' Games played in the streets of towns around Scotland; these are examples of medieval football games which are still played in towns in the United Kingdom and worldwide.

isle-of-man.title: Hop-tu-Naa
isle-of-man.summary: Hop-tu-Naa ( HOP choo NAY; Manx: Oie Houney; Irish: Oíche Shamhna [ˌiːçə ˈhəunˠə]) is a Celtic festival celebrated in the Isle of Man on 31 October. It is the celebration of the traditional Gaelic festival of Samhain, the start of winter.

isle-of-man.title: Hunt the Wren
isle-of-man.summary: Hunt the Wren (Manx: Shelg yn Dreean) is a traditional custom carried out on the Isle of Man on 26 December, Saint Stephen's Day. Traditionally, men and boys hunted a wren and placed it on top of a staff decorated with holly, ivy and ribbons, or displayed it in a decorated box on top of a pole.

isle-of-man.title: Tynwald Day
isle-of-man.summary: Tynwald Day (Manx: Laa Tinvaal) is the National Day of the Isle of Man.

isle-of-man.title: Yn Chruinnaght
isle-of-man.summary: Yn Chruinnaght (Manx for "the gathering") is a cultural festival in the Isle of Man which celebrates Manx music, Manx language and culture, and links with other Celtic cultures. The forerunner of Yn Chruinnaght was founded in 1924, and was known as Cruinnaght Vanninagh Ashoonagh ("Manx national gathering").

isle-of-man.title: Cammag
isle-of-man.summary: Cammag (Manx pronunciation: [ˈkʰamaɡ]) is a team sport originating on the Isle of Man. In modern times, an annual match of cammag is played in St John's on 26 December in keeping with this tradition.
